reason: The modifier 'inference-specific family' asserts inference-specificity for all three listed strategies, but the very same sentence immediately states that two of the three ('context/pipeline partitioning and expert parallelism both appear in training too') are not inference-specific. The label over-claims and is contradicted within one sentence; only P/D disaggregation is genuinely inference-specific.
evidence: chapter-10.md:9 'There is also an inference-specific family - context/pipeline partitioning, expert parallelism, and P/D disaggregation ... - repurposed here for serving; of the three, only P/D disaggregation has no training analogue (context/pipeline partitioning and expert parallelism both appear in training too).'

reason: Quote present at chapter-10 line 91. The gloss 'P-1 stage-slots are wasted out of the m.P slots' frames the bubble as a subtraction from the work-domain numerator (m.P), but the formula's denominator is time-domain (m+P-1); the two domains do not reconcile. The reviewer's P=4/m=8 check (11 time units for 32 useful, speedup 32/11) cannot be derived from the gloss as written, which implies m.P-(P-1). The formula and worked example are correct; only the verbal gloss misdescribes the denominator relationship.

Python: 32/11=2.909; 32/(32-3)=1.103; m+P-1=11.
